catalogue_requests.reason: cap.actuation.pump.v1 declares flow_rate and direction as command inputs, but nesp_lib.pump:Pump.run() takes no argument: it dispenses the volume, rate and direction that are configured on the pump (nesp_lib/pump.py:302-311), and those are writable state of this binding (cap.device.configure.v1). Expressing the class would need a per-call flow rate in uL/s converted to the pump's mL/min setting plus operator_required bounds in a second unit system. The extension keeps the pump's own vocabulary and is faithful to the upstream call.

no catalogue class purges a pump: the purge runs the pump at its maximum rate in the configured direction until it is stopped (Pump.run_purge, nesp_lib/pump.py:313-319), which no class in the catalogue describes. The action takes no input and reports the status the pump returns.

no catalogue class stops a syringe pump: the catalogue has no pump stop class (the stop classes cover motion and compute). The action takes no input, calls Pump.stop without waiting (STP, nesp_lib/pump.py:321-330) and is the declared safe-state action (safe_state=True) of this hardware R1 package.

notes:
The gate passed on the fake backend with no finding and no warning (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware was attached, native.py was never imported, no serial port was opened and no pump was run.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card is family-config with the SerialDriver helper (reason_code family:serial) and this package is a direct Driver over nesp_lib.pump:Pump with a native.py factory. A command table cannot express this pump: a request is assembled from parts (the address, a command letter code and formatted arguments, nesp_lib/pump.py:490-493) and in safe mode it is a binary frame of STX, a length byte, the request bytes, a CCITT CRC and ETX (nesp_lib/pump.py:527-543), while replies are framed in both modes (nesp_lib/pump.py:545-576). A maintainer should correct the card with an override.

NOT COVERED. (1) The serial wire protocol itself: the framing, the length byte and the CRC are produced and checked by the upstream library at run time; this package never builds or parses a frame, and the fake does not reproduce them, so no frame was checked. (2) The recording the card's mock_strategy.preferred names (transcript): the clone has no upstream tests, no hints and no recording, so the fake is an in-memory stand-in for the Pump object, not a replay of a recorded session; the card's second choice in the guide's order (a recording fake) is what this package has. (3) The heartbeat thread that safe mode starts (nesp_lib/pump.py:646-672): it lives inside the upstream object and the fake does not model it; setting safe_mode_timeout_s to a non-zero value would enable it on a real pump. (4) The settlement units the upstream setters choose (ML/UL for volume, MM/MH/UM/UH for rate, nesp_lib/pump.py:411-427): the driver writes the value in the pump's own unit and reads it back converted to millilitres and millilitres per minute. (5) firmware_upgrade, address, volume_infused_clear, volume_withdrawn_clear and the alarm status (StatusAlarmException) are not exposed. (6) The run and purge actions start the pump without waiting (Pump.run(False), README.md:101-106); their receipts do not claim that a dispense finished, which is reported by the state reads (status, running, volume_infused_ml, volume_withdrawn_ml).

BOUNDS. Two sourced limits: syringe_diameter_mm 0.1 to 80.0 mm from SYRINGE_DIAMETER_MINIMUM_MM and SYRINGE_DIAMETER_MAXIMUM_MM (nesp_lib/pump.py:30-33), and safe_mode_timeout_s 0 to 255 s from SAFE_MODE_TIMEOUT_DISABLED and SAFE_MODE_TIMEOUT_LIMIT_S (nesp_lib/pump.py:25-28); the setters of the clone refuse everything outside them. Two operator_required fields: pumping_volume_ml and pumping_rate_ml_per_min. The clone's own setter statements for those two are protocol envelopes, not device bounds: the volume is refused below 0.001/1000.0 mL and at or above 10_000.0 mL with an open upper edge (nesp_lib/pump.py:226-227) and the rate limits are dictated by the syringe diameter fitted (nesp_lib/pump.py:255), so the site states the range its syringe allows; site-limits.example.json is only an example overlay. pumping_direction is an enum (INFUSE or WITHDRAW), not a limit, so no overlay can widen it.

SAFETY. The pump is an actuator, so the package is R1 (above the card's R0 floor and the R1 floor of the pump class it maps). The native stop is Pump.stop(False), the STP command sent without waiting so an e-stop never waits for the pump; @estop and the safe-state action x-cap.florian-lapp.stop_pump.v1 use it. estop_physical_ref is not set because no line of the clone documents an independent hardware stop and SAFE-045 applies at R2 and above only. The hardware backend (native.py, pyserial, the serial port) was never run, and this package is model-authored with reviewed_by null and risk R1, so the loader of this SDK does not hold back its hardware backend the way it does at R2 and R3 -- enabling it stays an operator decision without any review protection from this package.

FAKE. fake.py is an in-memory stand-in for the Pump object. Its starting values are test data, each marked # placeholder: a real pump reports its own model, firmware, syringe diameter and settings, and its status changes only while it is pumping. It is not a recording of the device and it does not model the serial protocol or the heartbeat. gate.digest is the digest line the check printed (the report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-29; reviewed_by stays null): accepted after reviewer edits: risk raised from R1 to R2 (a pump that dispenses liquid, MHS/spec/04-safety.md), so the hardware backend waits for a human signature; native.py and facts.md now say so. The DEVIATION FROM THE CARD is accepted: a registry override now makes the card a direct driver. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
